title.narrative: MAP: Inclusive multi-stakeholder processes for transformation towards sustainable & resilient Food Systems (phase II))

description.narrative: Direct participants in Bolivia : 320 Personnel (30 government representatives, 30 representatives from multi stakeholder platforms, 100 representatives from the Private sector and 20 representatives from academia). Indirect target group of 39 100 persons (60% are women). These include vulnerable families from urban and peri urban districts of the municipality of La Paz, young women from socio economically deprived areas and peri urban producers, students, members of civil society organizations etc. Direct participants in Peru, 233 Person (43 representatives of the government, 74 multi stakeholder participants, 82 civil society, .21 representatives from the private sector, 7 representatives from the academia). Indirect target group: 81, 616 (55% women) Families who use the community kitchens and soup kitchens in the peri urban areas of Lima, consumers of organic markets, customers and consumers of the markets, owners of restaurants, children benefiting of the school feeding programs of Lima and Huanuco, producers in the valley of Lima and Huanuco, SMEs in the food chains in Huanuco.

Overall objective: Contribute to the strengthening of an enabling environment conducive for the realization of the right to adequate food in Bolivia and Peru."Projet objective: Public and private initiatives, through consolidated multi-stakeholder platforms (MAPs) in Bolivia (La Paz) and Peru (Huánuco and the Chillón River Valley), contribute to strengthening sustainable local food systems.Outcome 1: The capacities of organizations and other actors in local food systems to effectively participate in, guide, and contribute to the work and advocacy agendas of the multi-stakeholder platforms (MAPs) are strengthened."Outcome 2: Three prioritized multi-stakeholder platforms have an operational structure, possess updated work programs, and implement relevant measures to promote sustainable food systems.Outcome 3:Prototypes of innovative local models are implemented, scaled, or replicated. This is carried out with multi-stakeholder platforms, including partnerships with the private sector, in order to promote responsible, healthy, and sustainable food systems.

The transformation towards resilient and sustainable food systems requires a collaborative approach that engages society. Tools such as multi-stakeholder platforms are essential to identify gaps in food policies, facilitate dialogue between different actors and work together on sustainable solutions leading to inclusive policies. This is the second phase of the multi stakeholder platform project (PER1142) that was implemented between 2021-2023. Three multi stakeholder platforms will be prioritiezed in Peru (Chillon and Huanuc) and Boliiva (La Paz). The overall objective is to: Contribute to the strengthening of an enabling environment conducive for the realization of the right to adequate food in Bolivia and Peru.
